influences.name: Jacques Maritain
influences.context: In pursuing this path, Stravinsky was influenced substantially by Jacques Maritain (1882-1973), the Thomist philosopher who led a Catholic intellectual revival in France between the World Wars.

influences.name: G.K. Chesterton
influences.context: He speaks to the importance of tradition and the illusory nature of the "revolutionary" as applied to music; to amplify this, Stravinsky quotes G.K. Chesterton's paradox about revolution implying a return to its point of origin.

influences.name: Arnold Schoenberg
influences.context: Stravinsky's final religious compositions date from his "serial period," when he had begun to compose according to the ultra-modern twelve-tone method of Arnold Schoenberg.
